full_judgment:
Mr. Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman, J :- These three (3) appeals arises out of one order and decision dated 01.10.2002 passed by the Tribunal consisted of the Deputy Registrar of Trade Marks, Dhaka, disposing of three (3) opposition case being Opposition case Nos, 1808 of 2001, 1812 and 1821 of 2001 filed by the same set of appellants against same set of respondents arising out of three Trade Mark applications filed for granting Trade Mark "Banoful" being (i) T. M. Application No. 67307 in Class No. 30 for the product Chanchur. (however in the Trade Mark Journal the application is numbered as 67207); (ii) and T. M. Application No. 64277 in class No. 30 for the product sweetmeat; and (iii) T. M. Application No, 67306 in class No. 30 for the products Semai all filed by the respondent No. 1. rejecting the opposition cases and allowing the T. M. Applications. 

 3. The facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the appeals are that all the three cases are between the same parties and for the same Trade Mark "Baneful" but for different products. The appellants represent M/s. Baneful and co. of Chittagong and the contesting respondent represents baneful Abhijat Confectionery and Pasty Shop of Sylhet. In response to an advertisement published in the Trade Mark Journal for granting of Trade Mark "Banoful" for different products namely, Chanachur, Sweetmeat, semai on behalf of the contesting respondent, pursuant to orders passed by the office of the Trade Mark Registry, Dhaka, the appellants filed the aforesaid Opposition Cases objecting to prayer for granting of Trade Mark "Banoful" in favour of the contesting respondent contending amongst others, that the contesting respondent earlier become unsuccessful in his attempt to get registration of the Trade Mark "Baneful" in respect of various confectionery and sweetmeat items on the objection raised by the appellants hereof. The contesting respondent hereof went upto the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh and their lordships have found that the claim of the respondent as to the use of word "Banoful" since 1985 could not be proved. 

 5. The learned advocate appearing for the appellants in all the three appeals, taking us through the impugned judgment and order, by which three opposition cases No. 1808, 1818 and 1821 of 2001 have been disposed of,' submitted that the impugned judgment and order is bad in both in fact in law, inasmuch as the Deputy Registrar of Trade Marks as Tribunal passed the decision on misreading and misconstruing the statements made in the pleadings of the opposition cases and the counter statements filed three-against by the respondent No. I as well as the leave granting order passed by the Appellant Division in C. P. L. A. No. 1695 of 2001, preferred against the judgment and order passed in Trade Mark Appeal No.7 of 2000, by the respondent No.1 , and that the deputy Register of Trade , Marks as Tribunal in correctly mentioned that in the leave granting order the Appellate Division has found that the respondent no. 1 hereof has been in business using Trade Mark "Banoful" since 1985 and that the Appellate Division in its leave granting order has observed that the registration granted under Section-I0(2) of the Trade Marks Act in Opposition Case No. 1480 of 1998 and the order passed under Section-10(2) of the Trade Marks Act are not illegal and that the respondent No. I has been in "honest concurrent use" as , contemplated by Section-10(2) of the Trade Marks Act. 

 6. The learned Advocate in elaborating his submissions stated that the Tribunal below has purposely and malafide misquoted the leave granting order of the Appellate Division dated 11.03.2002 passed in C. P. L. A. No. 1695 of 2001 to justify the impugned order, The learned advocate further submitted that the Tribunal below did not consider of the judgments and orders of the High Court Division, though placed before him, wherein the claim of the contesting respondent hereof for the Trade Mark "Banoful" has been refused with categorical finding that the clime of prior use of the Trade Marks "Banoful" by the respondent No. 1 since 1985 was incorrect and fraudulent and that in three appeals namely, T.M.A No. 05 of 1996 T. M. A No. 07 of 2000. and T. M. A. No. 1 and 27 of 2001 the claim of the respondent No. 1 as prior user of Trade Mark "Banoful" 1985 has been found to be a false claim. The leave granting order in reference has been passed in one leave petition being CPLA No. 1695/2001 preferred against the judgment and order passed in T. M. A. No. 7 of 2000 of the High Court Division. The Tribunal below avoided to consider the fact that the operation of the Judgments and orders passed in T. M. A. Nos. 5 and 6 of 1996 as well as T. M. A. Nos. 1 and 27 of 2001 not being stayed the findings and decisions of those appeals are binding on the Tribunal, The Tribunal_ purposely ignored those decisions on the High Court Division in passing the impugned order holding that the respondent No. 1 is in "honest concurrent use" and "prior user since 1985", though the same are against materials on record. The learned advocate submitted that the Tribunal has found the respondents No. 1 as using the Trade Mark "Banoful" since 1985 relying on the statements made in the counter claim of the respondent No. 1 and that the Tribunal has erred in law in not considering that the period of illegal use of the Trade Mark "Banoful" since 1992, when litigation's started in between the same parties in respect of Trade Mark "Banoful", cannot be treated or counted as "period of use" for the purpose of application for the said Trade Mark "Banoful", in the eye of law and therefore the observation made by the Tribunal in the impugned decision order to the effect that both the parties have been carrying in their business for the last 14 years in respect of their items with the same Trade Mark "Banoful" and as such the question of confusion does not arise, cannot have any legal bearing. The learned advocate submitted that in view of the illegal use of the Trade Mark "Banoful" taking advantage of the litigation's the respondent no. 1 can not have any lawful claim as a "honest concurrent user" to get Trade Mark "Banoful" registered under section-10 (2) of the Trade Marks Act. The learned Advocate submitted that section-12 of the Trade Marks Act relates to the registration of Associated Trade Mark, which is nobody's case yet the Tribunal has passed an order under section-12 of the Trade Mark Act for granting Trade Mark "Banoful" in favour of the respondent no. 1 in three applications in reference rejecting the opposition cases. The learned advocate submitted that in view of the judgment and orders passed by the High court Division in the Trade Mark Appeals mentioned above, passing of any decision or order under section-25 of the Trade Mark Act by the Tribunal is neither called for nor has any relevance and as such the impugned decision and order passed for registration of Trade Mark "Banoful" in favour of the respondent No. 1 under section-10(2) and 25 of the Trade Marks Act in bad in the eye of law and cannot be sustained. 

 7. Mr. Gazi Md. Neamat Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 1 in T. M. Appeals No. 3,4 and 5 of 2003 i.e. in all the three appeals. Submitted that the Tribunal did not pass the impugned order in favour of the respondent no.1 as "prior user" but has passed the order under section-10(2) holding that the respondent no. 1 is in "honest concurrent use" of the Trade Mark "Banoful". The learned Advocate submitted that the Tribunal below considering the facts, circumstances and the materials available on record has passed the impugned order and that the rejection of the earlier payers for granting the Trade Mark "Banoful" in favour of the respondent no. 1 hereof have no relevance in the present cases in as much as those related to the other items and not related to the items like Chanachur, Semi and sweetmeat for which the pursuant proceeding were initiated. The learned advocate further submitted that the Tribunal below may have misquoted the leave granting order of the appellate Division passed in CPLA no. 1695 of 2001, in the impugned order but has rightly allowed the applications of the respondent no. 1 rejecting the opposition cases of the appellants under section-10(2) of the Trade Marks Act, as the respondent no. 1 is the concurrent user of the Trade Mark "Banoful" at least for the last 14 years, The learned advocate, however, denied that the impugned order has not been passed on the basis of "prior user" by the respondent No. 1, though that is the claim of the respondent no. 1 as to his use of the Trade Mark "Banoful" since 1985. 

 8. We have considered the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions of the learned advocates of the respective parties. We have also perused the impugned decision and order passed by the Deputy Registrar to Trade Marks as a Tribunal. It appears from the impugned decision and order the Tribunal has mentioned those documents of the appellants in the body of the impugned decision and order, which the Tribunal has considered in disposing of the opposition cases and thus it appears that the Tribunal, while passing the impugned decision and order, did not consider the judgments of the High Court Division passed in the Trade Mark Appeals referred to above and submitted by the appellants. The Tribunal however has taken-notice of submission of those judgments before the Tribunal, as appears from its order dated 15.09.2002, wherein the submissions made on behalf of the appellants and the respondent no.
